channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Putin Expresses Concern Over Declining Russian Culture in Central Asia at CIS Summit
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin voiced concerns at the CIS summit in Turkmenistan about the erosion of Russian culture and influence across member states. Despite the organization's history of inactivity, Putin promoted the CIS as a vehicle to maintain cultural and historical ties in Central Asia and the South Caucasus, highlighting a fear of losing cultural dominance.

item.title: Uzbekistan Marks 35 Years of Independence, Emphasizing Human Dignity as Development Basis
item.description: Uzbekistan celebrated its 35th anniversary of independence, with President Shavkat Mirziyoyev outlining strategic priorities for the next decade. The country has undergone significant transformations, prioritizing national values, historical memory, economic opportunities, and human interests. The principle of 'For the sake of human honor and dignity' guides reforms, aiming to protect citizens' rights and improve living conditions.

item.title: Firearms Used in Altercation in Zharkent, Kazakhstan; Criminal Case Opened
item.description: A criminal case is being investigated following an incident in Zharkent, Kazakhstan, where firearms were used during an altercation between men. Police have initiated cases for hooliganism and attempted murder. One 33-year-old man was hospitalized with gunshot wounds. Authorities have confiscated a weapon and arrested two suspects.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Belgium Leaders Discuss AI's Impact on Higher Education at Forum
item.description: The Rector's Forum, attended by leaders of Kazakh and Belgian higher education institutions, convened at the Alem.ai international center. Discussions focused on the impact of artificial intelligence on education and scientific research. Participants explored Kazakhstan's role as a regional hub and the integration of AI in academic and educational processes. Several agreements were signed to expand partnerships.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Finance Ministry Assures Tax System Resilience Amid Russian Service Disruptions
item.description: Kazakhstan's Finance Minister Madi Takiev stated that the national tax reporting system operates on the ministry's own servers and databases, with backups in place. He confirmed that taxpayers do not use systems like 1C-Accounting for state settlements. This assurance follows disruptions to Russian services like Yandex Go, which affected some taxi and delivery components operating outside Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Maslikhat Elections May Cost More Than Kurultai Elections, Says CEC Member
item.description: A member of Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission (CEC), Mikhail Bortnik, explained that elections for maslikhats (local representative bodies) could be more expensive than Kurultai elections. This is due to the involvement of 3,022 district election commissions. Funds for these extraordinary elections will be allocated from the government's reserve budget, as they were not initially included in the Republic of Kazakhstan's budget.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Deputy PM Defends Tax Reform Amid Budget Shortfall Concerns
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin stated the tax reform has met expectations, generating 3 trillion tenge in additional budget revenue over nine months. Despite a VAT shortfall, he argued the reform is the economy's sole cash source and performing well, projecting at least 3.6 trillion tenge by year-end.

item.title: Kazakhstan Rescuers Train for Earthquake Response in CSTO Drills in Tajikistan
item.description: Rescuers from Kazakhstan's 'Barys' Republican Emergency Service are participating in Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) exercises in Tajikistan, practicing responses to devastating earthquakes. The drills focus on search and rescue, command and control, and inter-agency coordination to enhance readiness for large-scale emergencies.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Germany Enhance Cooperation in Quality Infrastructure Development
item.description: Uzbekistan and Germany are expanding their collaboration in developing a national quality infrastructure. A meeting between officials from Uzbekistan's Agency for Technical Regulation and Germany's 'Support for Reforms in the National Quality Infrastructure' project focused on harmonizing legislation with WTO requirements, improving product safety, and boosting export capabilities. Agreements were reached to further develop the national quality infrastructure and jointly prepare for World Quality Week in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Educational Cooperation with Canadian Universities
item.description: Uzbekistan is broadening its educational ties with Canadian universities. Meetings focused on increasing admission opportunities for Uzbek students into Canadian institutions, including scholarships and special admission terms. Discussions also covered professional development courses for school consultants and teachers, and the signing of memorandums of cooperation. These initiatives aim to enhance international educational prospects for Uzbek students and improve teacher qualifications.

item.title: Kazakhstan President, Belgian King and Queen Attend Forum of Rectors on AI in Education
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, along with the King and Queen of Belgium, participated in a forum of rectors focused on the impact of artificial intelligence on education and research. The event explored AI's role in higher education and science, Kazakhstan's position as a regional hub, and opportunities for collaboration between Kazakh and Belgian universities. Several agreements were signed.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Belgium Collaborate on AI Projects for Education and Disease Diagnosis
item.description: Kazakhstan and Belgium are developing joint artificial intelligence projects focused on improving education and enabling early diagnosis of Parkinson's disease. These initiatives, presented to leaders of both nations, stem from collaboration between scientists and involve research in AI, neuroscience, and adaptive learning, as well as methods for early Parkinson's detection.

item.title: Kuwaiti Airline Plans to Resume Flights to Kazakhstan Upon Regional Stabilization
item.description: Kuwait's Jazeera Airways is ready to resume direct flights to Kazakhstan once the regional situation stabilizes, according to the Kazakh Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The airline previously operated flights between Kuwait and Almaty in 2021 but suspended them due to regional instability. Resumption is expected to boost tourism and trade.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economic Growth to Outpace China and India by 2026, UN Forecasts
item.description: The UN forecasts that Kyrgyzstan's economy will grow by 8.8% in 2026, surpassing the growth rates of China and India. This projected expansion is expected to position Kyrgyzstan among the fastest-developing economies in the region. The forecast highlights significant economic momentum for the Central Asian nation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Lowering Initial Mortgage Down Payment
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has instructed the Financial Market Regulation Agency and the Ministry of Industry and Construction to develop proposals for reducing the initial down payment for mortgages. This initiative aims to improve housing finance mechanisms and support the construction sector's goal of completing 20.4 million square meters of housing by 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan Awards Winners of International Robotics Tournament and Their Coaches
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan has awarded medals to the winners of the international robotics tournament 'FIRST Global Challenge' and their coaches. The awards recognize their high intellectual potential, professional skills, and significant contribution to raising Uzbekistan's international prestige. The tournament, held in South Korea, featured gifted youth from nearly 190 countries.

item.title: Audits in Social Health Insurance Fund Prevented Losses of 23.4 Billion Tenge
item.description: Audits within the Social Health Insurance Fund (FSMС) have prevented financial losses amounting to 23.4 billion tenge over nine months. Kazakhstan's Minister of Finance, Madie Zholmanov, stated that enhanced monitoring and anti-fraud controls were implemented, particularly focusing on procurement and payment of medical services. The fund received over 1 trillion tenge from the state budget.

item.title: Freedom Holding Corp. Expands Global Ecosystem Beyond Kazakhstan, Faces Russian Prosecutor General's Lawsuit
item.description: Freedom Holding Corp., primarily operating in Kazakhstan, is expanding its business into Europe, the US, and Asia, recently acquiring a Turkish bank and reporting a 40% revenue increase. Concurrently, Russia's Prosecutor General's Office has filed a lawsuit against the group. The holding company, registered in Nevada and traded on Nasdaq, operates in 24 countries with 264 offices.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports Over 13 Million Square Meters of Housing Completed
item.description: Kazakhstan's construction sector saw an 11.5% growth in the first nine months, reaching 7.8 trillion tenge. Housing completions increased by 2.7% to 13.2 million square meters during the same period. The Vice-Minister of Industry and Construction, Kuan­dyk K­azhkenov, noted positive dynamics in most regions, with significant growth in the Ulytau region, Atyrau region, and Shymkent city. Seventeen regions recorded housing growth.

item.title: Kazakhstan-Belgian AI and Mathematics Lab Launched at Alem.ai
item.description: A joint Kazakhstan-Belgian AI and mathematics laboratory was presented at the international AI center Alem.ai. Initiatives include NeuroLearn for AI, neuroscience, and adaptive learning research, and ParkScreen for AI methods in early Parkinson's screening. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and King Philippe of Belgium attended the presentation. The lab aims to foster collaboration in AI and mathematics.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prime Minister Orders Reduction in Mortgage Down Payment Requirements
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has instructed a reduction in the initial down payment for mortgages in Kazakhstan. This measure is part of a broader plan to increase housing accessibility for citizens by 2026, aiming to put 20.4 million square meters of housing into use with necessary infrastructure. The Finance Market Regulation and Development Agency will propose specific mechanisms for lowering the down payment.

item.title: Kazakhstan Official Identifies Reason for Sharp Price Increases
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy, Serik Zhumangarin, cited a sharp rise in consumer lending, particularly unsecured loans, as a primary cause of recent price hikes. He explained that increased consumer spending, fueled by easy credit, drove up demand and prices, especially for imported goods. Stricter macroprudential requirements have since cooled the market.

item.title: Uzbekistan Showcases Mining Technologies in Japan
item.description: Uzbekistan presented its advanced mining technologies at a presentation in Japan focused on remote sensing for sustainable mineral extraction and geological exploration. The event, part of JICA's knowledge-sharing programs, included participants from various countries. Uzbekistan highlighted its achievements in mining, mineral resources, and economic potential, emphasizing gold, uranium, copper, and lithium extraction, and modernization efforts.

item.title: Kazakhstan Imports Over 9,000 Head of Breeding Cattle
item.description: Kazakhstan has imported more than 9,000 head of breeding cattle since the beginning of the year, according to the Vice-Minister of Agriculture, Azat Sultanov. An additional 16,000 head of cattle and 7,000 sheep are currently undergoing selection and quarantine. The country is also implementing a program to expand dairy farms.

item.title: King of Belgium Urges Businesses to Expand Cooperation with Kazakhstan
item.description: King Philippe of Belgium has called on businesses in Kazakhstan and Belgium to enhance cooperation in energy, critical minerals, transport, logistics, finance, and tourism. Speaking at the fourth session of the Kazakh-Belgian Business Council, he highlighted the potential for strengthening ties between Europe and Central Asia, with Belgium serving as a gateway to the EU market.

item.title: Euronews Features Kazakhstan's Historic Underground Mosques on UNESCO Heritage List
item.description: Euronews has published a feature on Kazakhstan's historical heritage, highlighting ancient architectural monuments, including five underground mosques dating from the 12th to 18th centuries. These sites, now part of Kazakhstan's new UNESCO World Heritage nominations, preserve Sufi traditions and ancient beliefs. The report aims to showcase the country's rich history and spiritual legacy to an international audience.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev to Visit Azerbaijan for CICA Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will pay a working visit to Azerbaijan on October 14-15. He will participate in the seventh summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Baku.

item.title: Tajikistan's Fall Conscription Plan Achieves 84% Fulfillment in Ten Days
item.description: In the first ten days of the fall conscription for Tajikistan's Armed Forces, the recruitment plan reached 84% completion. The Ministry of Defense reported on October 12 that over 40 cities and districts had fully met their fall conscription targets ahead of schedule. Previously, the ministry had announced 55% of the plan was fulfilled on the first day.

item.title: Uzbek President to Attend CICA Summit in Baku for Working Visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Azerbaijan on October 14-15 for a working trip. He will participate in the 7th summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Baku. The summit agenda includes strengthening confidence, ensuring peace and security in Asia, and institutional development of CICA. Bilateral meetings with foreign leaders are also planned.

item.title: Afghan Foreign Minister Meets Qatar Envoy to Discuss International Ties
item.description: Afghanistan's Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi met with Qatar's ambassador to Kabul, Mirdif Al-Qashouti, to discuss strengthening bilateral relations and expanding Afghanistan's engagement with the international community. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated the meeting focused on Qatar's efforts to facilitate the Islamic Emirate's international engagement. Qatar reaffirmed its commitment to supporting these efforts.

item.title: Zelensky Accuses Russia of Violating Agreement Not to Strike Energy Facilities
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of not adhering to an agreement with former US President Donald Trump to cease air strikes on energy infrastructure. European officials are seeking clarification on this agreement and another concerning Russian diesel exports. Zelensky stated that while Ukraine avoided striking Russian oil refineries, Russia continued to attack Ukrainian energy and critical infrastructure.

item.title: Emomali Rahmon Inaugurates Training Center Facilities and Oversees CSTO Joint Exercises in Shahrituz
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon of Tajikistan inaugurated several facilities at the Civil Defense Committee's training center in Shahrituz district. He also observed joint Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) exercises. Additionally, other social facilities were opened during his visit to the region.

item.title: BBC Publishes Final Interview of Slain Russian Journalist Anna Politkovskaya
item.description: The BBC released a final interview with renowned Russian journalist and human rights advocate Anna Politkovskaya, who was assassinated on October 7, 2006. Politkovskaya was known for her investigations into human rights abuses in Chechnya and her criticism of the Russian government. The interview was originally broadcast in English in November 2006.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sets November 29, 2026, for Early Elections of Local Assembly Deputies
item.description: Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission has scheduled early elections for all levels of local assemblies (maslikhats) for November 29, 2026. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev previously signed a decree to prematurely terminate the powers of all maslikhats, citing changes in the party system. The elections will select 3,447 deputies for 228 local representative bodies.

item.title: Piskent District Head Reprimanded for Insulting Farmers
item.description: The head of Piskent district, Muzaffar Aripov, received a reprimand for violating ethical conduct and professional ethics. This action followed the spread of an audio recording where he allegedly insulted farmers and threatened to confiscate their land. The district administration acknowledged inappropriate communication.

item.title: Uzbek doctor saves passenger's life on Tashkent-Seoul flight
item.description: An Uzbek doctor, Hasan Kamilov, saved a female passenger's life on an Uzbekistan Airways flight from Tashkent to Seoul. The passenger's condition rapidly deteriorated, with no detectable blood pressure or pulse. Dr. Kamilov administered emergency aid using his personal medication and onboard supplies, allowing the flight to continue.

item.title: Kazakhstan reports nearly 6 million tons of oil production losses amid CPC and Tengiz issues
item.description: Kazakhstan experienced oil production losses of up to 5.9 million tons, though some volumes were recovered. The Ministry of Energy stated that planned maintenance was postponed at Kashagan and Tengiz fields to compensate. Negotiations are underway to increase production. Losses have been reduced to 1.9 million tons.

item.title: Former Afghan diplomat Aziz Boriz lauds launch of Asia-Plus Persian service
item.description: Aziz Boriz, a former Afghan diplomat and head of a UK-based research center, has praised the launch of the Persian service by Asia-Plus news agency. He described it as a strategic move that will aid in the unity and recognition of Farsi speakers worldwide regarding Tajikistan.

item.title: Former Helmand military official's body found six months after Taliban arrest
item.description: Taliban sources in Helmand report that the body of a former local police commander, Allahdad Badizi, has been returned to his family. He was arrested by Taliban intelligence six months prior, despite initial denials of his detention. He was reportedly tortured in prison.

item.title: Afghanistan and Iran discuss expanding industrial and mining cooperation
item.description: Iran's ambassador to Kabul met with officials from the Afghanistan Chamber of Industries and Mines to explore enhancing economic ties, joint investments, and strengthening collaboration in the industrial and mining sectors. The Afghan deputy for industry highlighted existing opportunities for cooperation.
